notable.note: The single most useful file in this batch for management, none of it about a prospect. Six findings, all quoted. (1) Income qualification is being done with ChatGPT: of a commercial diver, 'when I put that into ChatGPT, it said he was probably making around 75k, around there', and of the 23-year-old firefighter, 'I once again chat GPT'd, like, estimated salary for a five-year firefighter, and it said that would be around 60k'. Financial qualification is a job-title lookup, not a conversation. (2) No clinical screening exists at the setting stage and the setter says so: about a prospect whose back is 'blown out', 'I don't actually think I asked many questions about whether he's actually good to start training now. So that's funny on me.' The closer agrees the injury is 'a little bit of a red flag' — and this is the same gap that goes unaddressed on the Scott Hamilton, Rudolph, Javier and Angelo calls in this batch. (3) A knowingly low-intent lead was booked deliberately: 'this is one of those guys who I knew had the money, but I financially qualified. I had him regardless, just like, because I almost wanted him to DQ himself, he was that low-intent.' (4) The $100 deposit is a systematic tactic, not a one-off: 'those two that I did at down payment earlier today', and the closer's frustration that it is all he is getting — 'the Andrew is closing 6K [paid in full] and I'm just getting down payments and whatever. Annoying.' (5) The closer is under explicit cash pressure that he ties directly to how he sells: 'I want to get to the 50K, and that means I have to do another 24K, my projection is 22, and I'm only at 12 so far', 'I need to get the cash', and of the injured firefighter, 'I will do my best to sell him on something.' (6) Call-taking is being triaged by expected wallet size: 'if someone is a commercial diver, I think they do make money... I'll sort of screw up my sleep for one day, but with someone that's like mid intent, don't even do it please.'

quality.notes: Two speakers with the closer labelled correctly, so attribution is better than in the sales calls, but overlapping speech causes real problems. At 00:05:31 and 00:09:32 both speakers' lines are merged into single blocks with identical timestamps; at 00:11:09-00:11:28 the exchange about the firefighter interleaves wrongly so the closer's and setter's assessments are swapped; and at 00:06:06 the setter's ChatGPT salary estimate runs into the closer's reply. The setter is identified only from the file title. Several names are garbled or uncertain — 'Montana' and 'Discord' both appear to be mis-transcriptions of the same prospect's name.
